 BCCI explores two new IPL franchises ahead of 2028 season: Reports
 Pune and Vadodara are among the cities being considered as potential homes for the new teams 
 by
 e4m Staff
 Published: 
 Nov 10, 2026 8:27 PM 
 | 
 1 min read 
 Follow Us 
 The Indian Premier League (IPL) could increase its team count from 10 to 12 starting with the 2028 season, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) reportedly weighing a proposal to introduce two additional franchises, according to media reports.
 According to media reports, Pune and Vadodara are among the cities being considered as potential homes for the new teams. However, the discussions are understood to be at an initial stage, with no final decision taken on the locations.
 --> 
 --> 
 The proposed expansion is expected to coincide with the IPL's next media rights cycle, spanning 2028 to 2032. Each of the new franchises could be valued at over $1 billion, with domestic and overseas investors, including private equity funds, sovereign wealth funds and prominent business groups, reportedly showing interest.
 --> 
 -->
 The BCCI's plans will depend on several factors, including the commercial feasibility of expanding the tournament, broadcaster interest and the availability of leading Indian players.
